utility.notes: The City of Citrus Heights' own solar permit page requires 'SMUD interconnection pre-approval' as part of the submittal process, directly confirming SMUD as the electric utility.

value.name: Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD)
value.notes: SMUD is a vertically-integrated municipal utility — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA, consistent with the pattern already established for other SMUD-territory records this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Citrus Heights Community Development Department

interconnection_url.notes: The city's page requires SMUD interconnection pre-approval but does not itself provide a direct link to SMUD's interconnection page.

battery_programs.notes: The statewide SGIP program (administered by the CPUC-regulated IOUs) does not apply to SMUD customers, since SMUD is a municipal utility outside CPUC jurisdiction, consistent with other SMUD-territory records this session.

other_conditions: PV system must be installed on a permitted main dwelling rooftop only — no trenching allowed, no ballasted systems
No main panel upgrades allowed through SolarAPP+
New ADU systems cannot use the SolarAPP+ platform
Properties in flood zones must use an alternative (non-SolarAPP+) submittal process
Contractor must hold a California C-10, C-46, or B license classification, be registered with SolarAPP+, and hold a valid CSLB license and City business license
Permit expediters are prohibited without written contractor authorization

permit_fees.notes: The page states a processing fee (via SolarAPP+/invoice) applies and re-inspection fees apply for documentation failures, but no dollar amounts are given.
